record.paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
record.context_brief: Distinguish two equivalent quasi-norms on L^{APP}_z.
record.original_question: Find a shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0) and an operator S in L^{APP}_z(X,Y) for some Banach spaces X,Y such that the two equivalent quasi-norms on L^{APP}_z introduced in Theorem 1.4, namely ||S|L^{APP}_z|| based on the dyadic approximation numbers and |||S|L^{APP}_z||| based on z-representations, are not actually equal on that operator.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. A sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of the space of bounded scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$ that is solid (if $|a_n|\le|b_n|$ for all $n$ and $(b_n)\in z$, then $(a_n)\in z$) and equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\,|z\|$ making it a quasi-Banach sequence space in which the unit vectors $e_n$ are bounded. Such a sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is called shift-monotone if the dyadic block-shift operators are bounded, i.e. there is a constant $c\ge 1$ such that for every $(\xi_n)\in z$ one has $\|(\xi_{2n})|z\|\le c\,\|(\xi_n)|z\|$ and $\|(\xi_{n})|z\|\le c\,\|(\xi_{n/2})|z\|$ in the appropriate sense (so that passage between sequences indexed by $n$ and by dyadic blocks $2^k\le n<2^{k+1}$ is bounded).

For Banach spaces $X,Y$ and a bounded linear operator $S\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$, the $n$-th approximation number is 
$$a_n(S)=\inf\{\|S-A\|: A\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y),\ \mathrm{rank}\,A<n\},\qquad n\ge 1,$$
and the dyadic approximation numbers are $a^{(d)}_k(S)=a_{2^k}(S)$ for $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$.

Given a shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, define the approximation operator ideal $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$ as the class of operators $S\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ such that the dyadic approximation sequence $(a^{(d)}_k(S))_{k\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ belongs to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, with quasi-norm
$$\|S\,|\,\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\|:=\bigl\|(a^{(d)}_k(S))_{k\in\mathbb{N}_0}\,\big|\,z\bigr\|.$$

A $z$-representation of $S\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ is a series representation $S=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} S_k$ converging in operator norm, where each $S_k\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ has finite rank $\mathrm{rank}\,S_k<2^k$, such that the sequence $(\|S_k\|)_{k\in\mathbb{N}_0}\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$. Define
$$|\!|\!|S\,|\,\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|\!|\!|:=\inf\bigl\|(\|S_k\|)_{k\in\mathbb{N}_0}\,\big|\,z\bigr\|,$$
where the infimum is taken over all $z$-representations of $S$. It is known that $\|\cdot\,|\,\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\|$ and $|\!|\!|\cdot\,|\,\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|\!|\!|$ are equivalent quasi-norms on $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$.

Problem. Exhibit a shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, Banach spaces $X,Y$, and an operator $S\in\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z(X,Y)$ for which the two equivalent quasi-norms above are not equal, i.e.
$$\|S\,|\,\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\|\ \neq\ |\!|\!|S\,|\,\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|\!|\!|.$$
